title: Check yourself: Discovery, the record and one decision for two audiences

questions.stem: Scenario: Priya compares four designs for a call-centre assistant. Two of them meet every service level, one at 90,000 a month and one at 140,000. A third costs 40,000 but misses the latency target. Which does the record recommend?

options.text: The cheaper of the two that qualify, since price decides among them
options.says: A design must qualify first, and among those that do, the cheapest is recommended.

options.text: The 140,000 design, because the larger budget leaves room to grow beyond the target
options.says: Ruled out because "the newest" and "the most capable" are not criteria, as "the cheapest one that meets the service levels" is.

options.text: The 40,000 design, because it is the cheapest of the four and the target can be tuned later
options.says: Ruled out because "An option that misses a service level is not a candidate, however cheap".

options.text: Both of the designs that meet every level, so that the sponsor can pick the one preferred
options.says: Ruled out because "Two recommended options push the choice back to the reader".

origin.section: Options, and the rule for the recommendation

questions.stem: Scenario: Hugo must brief a sponsor who will decide in one meeting on whether a pilot goes ahead. Hugo's draft is six pages of tables, ending with the break-even derivation. What should the first page of the record hold?

options.text: The derivation of the break-even, which is the reason for every later number
options.says: Ruled out because "The summary is first because the sponsor stops reading early".

options.text: The table by segment, so the sponsor sees the accuracy figures before anything else
options.says: Ruled out because the table by segment belongs with "the numbers that produced it" for the engineer.

options.text: A short summary in plain words, covering the cost, the risk and the decision requested
options.says: The sponsor stops reading early, so the summary comes first and ends in the decision.

options.text: The list of the model's settings, so the sponsor can confirm the configuration
options.says: Ruled out because the sponsor's summary has "no percentages of percentages, no model names".
